[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Self-Supervised Learning in Computer Vision: SimCLR, CLIP, and DINO"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) has revolutionized computer vision by enabling models to learn rich, transferable representations from unlabeled data. This tutorial explores three foundational architectures: SimCLR (contrastive learning), CLIP (vision-language alignment), and DINO (self-distillation without negative pairs)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. SimCLR: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"SimCLR relies on data augmentation to create positive pairs. Two distorted views of the same image are passed through a base encoder and a projection head. The NT-Xent (normalized temperature-scaled cross entropy) loss maximizes agreement between positive pairs while pushing apart negative pairs."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def nt_xent_loss(z_i, z_j, temperature=0.5):
    batch_size = z_i.size(0)
    z = torch.cat([z_i, z_j], dim=0)
    sim_matrix = F.cosine_similarity(z.unsqueeze(1), z.unsqueeze(0), dim=2)
    sim_matrix = sim_matrix / temperature
    
    # Mask out self-similarity
    mask = torch.eye(2 * batch_size, device=z.device).bool()
    sim_matrix.masked_fill_(mask, -float('inf'))
    
    labels = torch.cat([
        torch.arange(batch_size, 2 * batch_size),
        torch.arange(batch_size)
    ], dim=0).to(z.device)
    
    return F.cross_entropy(sim_matrix, labels)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. CLIP: Connecting Text and Images"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) trains an image encoder and a text encoder jointly to predict which images correspond to which captions in a batch. This zero-shot capability allows models to generalize to downstream classification tasks without fine-tuning."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Image Encoder: Typically a Vision Transformer (ViT) or ResNet."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Text Encoder: A Transformer model processing tokenized text descriptions."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Objective: Symmetric cross-entropy loss over the cosine similarity matrix of image and text embeddings."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. DINO: Self-Distillation with Vision Transformers"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"DINO (Self-distillation with no labels) interprets self-supervised learning as a self-distillation task. It uses a teacher and a student network where the student learns to predict the output of the teacher without requiring negative pairs, preventing collapse through centering and sharpening techniques."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"import torch

def dino_loss(student_output, teacher_output, temperature_s=0.1, temperature_t=0.04, center=None):
    student_out = student_output / temperature_s
    if center is not None:
        teacher_out = (teacher_output - center) / temperature_t
    else:
        teacher_out = teacher_output / temperature_t
    
    loss = -torch.sum(torch.softmax(teacher_out, dim=-1) * torch.log_softmax(student_out, dim=-1), dim=-1)
    return loss.mean()"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"SimCLR, CLIP, and DINO represent major milestones in computer vision. SimCLR established strong contrastive baselines, CLIP bridged computer vision with natural language processing, and DINO unlocked emergent semantic segmentation properties in Vision Transformers."}]
